parole.testo: From Middle English drivel, probably from driven + -el, unless borrowed from an equivalent word in another West Germanic language. Compare Old Dutch drevel (“scullion”).

parole.significato: A comb used to separate flax fibers.
parole.testo: From Middle English hechele, of West Germanic origin, related to the root of hook. Doublet of hackle and heckle.

parole.significato: The fruit of forest-trees (beech, oak, chestnut, pecan, etc.), especially if having fallen from the tree, used as fodde…
parole.testo: From Old English mæst (“fallen nuts, food for swine”) and mæstan (“to fatten”), from West Germanic; probably related to meat.

parole.significato: The border of an article of clothing doubled back and stitched together to finish the edge and prevent it from fraying.
parole.testo: From Middle English hem, hemm, in turn from Old English hem, of West Germanic origin, from Proto-West Germanic *hammjan from Proto-Germanic *hamjaną.
